author: Alex M Shepherd (Flickr user 137390807@N03, https://www.flickr.com/people/137390807@N03/)
license: CC0 1.0 Universal (Flickr 'Public Domain Dedication (CC0)'); no attribution required
subspecies_or_sex_if_stated: not stated (adult; glossy head, yellow bill, spangled undertail; photographer caption 'Starling garden 20 5 2020 4a'; taken 2020-05-20)
symmetry_note: Best symmetry in the set. Perpendicular half-spans from the bill-to-tail-centre axis 968 px vs 976 px (about 1 pct difference; axis hand-placed, +/-3 pct). Both wings fully extended with every primary tip visible, tail fully fanned and centred on the axis. Body axis rotated about 17 deg from horizontal in frame; head slightly foreshortened. Tip-to-tip 1978 px. Plain pale-blue sky, background residual after plane fit very low.
why_kept: Cleanest symmetric full-spread ventral frame: sharp, whole bird 187 px from nearest edge, plain sky, adult plumage unambiguous.
species_check: Zoom 4.4x head: yellow bill, glossy black head with fine buff speckling, round dark eye. Zoom 3.5x tail: short fanned tail of square-tipped feathers, buff-edged spangled undertail coverts. Zoom 5.4x on both wingtips: all primaries complete, sharp, uncropped. Triangular pointed wings. Consistent with Sturnus vulgaris in spangled/glossy adult plumage; no myna/unicolor features.

author: Alex M Shepherd (Flickr user 137390807@N03, https://www.flickr.com/people/137390807@N03/)
license: CC0 1.0 Universal (Flickr 'Public Domain Dedication (CC0)'); no attribution required
subspecies_or_sex_if_stated: not stated (moulting juvenile per photographer caption 'Starling juvenile moulting garden 1 8 2024 3a'; taken 2024-08-01)
symmetry_note: Half-spans 960 px vs 1065 px (about 5 pct, lower wing on image-left shorter; axis hand-placed). Body axis horizontal. Both wings fully extended; tail fully fanned. Upper wingtip is only 14 px from the top frame edge (complete but tight). Outermost primaries on the lower-left wing are motion-soft. Tip-to-tip 2074 px. Plain blue sky with a slight vignette gradient.
why_kept: Juvenile plumage example with a large, near-symmetric spread; useful for colour-agnostic outline fitting.
species_check: Zoom 4.4x head: uniform pale brown head and breast, dark pointed bill, dark eye with pale eye-ring edge (juvenile starling). Zoom 3.7x tail: fanned brown tail, dark moult-patch feathers with white spots on flank. Zoom 5.4x wingtips: lower-left tip soft (motion), upper tip complete but near the frame edge. Juvenile Sturnus vulgaris cues: dull brown plumage, white spots appearing in moult, short square tail, triangular wings. Caveat: plain juvenile plumage cannot by itself exclude a juvenile spotless starling; ruled out by range (photographer's captions point to Scotland), not by plumage.

author: Alex M Shepherd (Flickr user 137390807@N03, https://www.flickr.com/people/137390807@N03/)
license: CC0 1.0 Universal (Flickr 'Public Domain Dedication (CC0)'); no attribution required
subspecies_or_sex_if_stated: not stated (adult; photographer caption 'Starling in flight garden 23 5 2025 2a'; taken 2025-05-23)
symmetry_note: Half-spans 2032 px vs 1753 px (about 7 pct; upper wing slightly more foreshortened, slight bank). Body axis about 11 deg from horizontal. Both wings extended and swept back; tail fully fanned; feet tucked at the tail base (small bump on the outline). Tip-to-tip 4276 px, largest in the set. Plain pale-blue sky.
why_kept: Very high resolution adult glide with fully visible primaries; mild bank only.
species_check: Zoom 2.9x head: yellow bill with dark base, glossy purple-green black head. Zoom 2.4x tail: fanned, finely barred tail with spangled buff-edged undertail coverts. Zoom 3.7x wingtips: both complete; outer primaries thin and slightly soft. Sturnus vulgaris adult glossy/spangled plumage.

author: Pierre-Marie Epiney (Flickr https://www.flickr.com/people/83657186@N05)
subspecies_or_sex_if_stated: not stated (spangled post-moult plumage, dark bill; taken 2023-09-26)
symmetry_note: Half-spans 677 px vs 550 px (about 10 pct; the raised upper wing is foreshortened, bird banked slightly). Body axis about 17 deg from horizontal. Both wings extended with tips visible; tail only partly fanned. Tip-to-tip 1239 px. Saturated uniform deep-blue sky.
why_kept: Only Commons-hosted full-spread ventral frame; strong contrast (dark bird, saturated sky); winter-type spangling is clear.
species_check: Zoom 4.4x head: dark pointed bill, pale supercilium over dark eye-stripe, whole head covered in buff-white spots (winter plumage). Zoom 3.7x tail: short tail with buff-edged undertail coverts, a few rectrices spread. Zoom 5.4x wingtips: complete; some JPEG blocking and sharpening halo visible. Sturnus vulgaris non-breeding plumage.

author: Alex M Shepherd (Flickr user 137390807@N03, https://www.flickr.com/people/137390807@N03/)
license: CC0 1.0 Universal (Flickr 'Public Domain Dedication (CC0)'); no attribution required
subspecies_or_sex_if_stated: not stated (juvenile per caption 'Starling juveniles West Links 14 7 2022 2a'; taken 2022-07-14)
symmetry_note: Half-spans 440 px vs 499 px (about 6 pct; hand-placed axis, tail partly spread). Body axis about 12 deg from horizontal. Both wings extended; lower-left outermost primary is a thin, slightly soft streak. Tip-to-tip 1184 px. Plain pale blue-grey sky, slight gradient. TWO BIRDS IN FRAME: a second juvenile sits in the lower half and does not touch the first; the kept bird is the upper one, bbox x 922-1934, y 155-920 (second bird bbox x 1126-2223, y 1170-1763). Crop to the upper bird before segmenting.
why_kept: Second juvenile glide with near-symmetric spread and clean sky; adds a duller-plumage silhouette. Needs a crop because of the second bird.
species_check: Zoom 4.4x head: uniform brown head, dark bill, dark eye with black eye-stripe, pale throat (juvenile). Zoom 3.7x tail: partly fanned brown tail with white-tipped underside. Zoom 5.4x wingtips: complete; lower-left outer primary slender and slightly soft. Juvenile Sturnus vulgaris. Caveat: plain juvenile plumage cannot by itself exclude a juvenile spotless starling; ruled out by range (photographer's captions point to Scotland), not by plumage.

author: Alex M Shepherd (Flickr user 137390807@N03, https://www.flickr.com/people/137390807@N03/)

symmetry_note: Half-spans 1159 px vs 1506 px (about 13 pct; bank, upper wing foreshortened). Body axis about 31 deg from horizontal. Both wings extended; outline carries two non-bird features: a food item in the bill and legs/feet hanging below the body (landing approach). Tip-to-tip 2814 px. Plain blue sky.
why_kept: Large, sharp and fully spread, but banked about 13 pct and the legs and food item alter the outline; mask them out or prefer 01-05.
species_check: Zoom 4.4x head: glossy black head with iridescent sheen, bill gripping a pale grub and green item. Zoom 3.7x tail: spangled undertail coverts with buff chevrons, pink legs, fanned tail. Zoom 5.2x wingtips: all primaries complete and sharp. Sturnus vulgaris adult.

author: James Johnstone from Ecclefechan, Scotland (Flickr https://www.flickr.com/people/89786933@N02, photo https://www.flickr.com/photos/jetjohn/35494562761/)
symmetry_note: Phase: wings raised and spread at the top of the downstroke. Bird is seen head-on from below (nose toward camera), so the body axis is foreshortened (bill-to-tail length 378 px vs wingspan 1674 px). Half-spans 862 px vs 753 px (about 7 pct) but the two wings are not at the same elevation (left wing raised about 40 deg, right nearer horizontal), so a slight roll. Tip-to-tip 1676 px. Pale lilac-grey sky; the bottom 30 pct of the frame has foliage but is well clear of the bird.
why_kept: Best symmetric head-on raised-wing frame found; heavy noise and tone processing, body axis foreshortened and a slight roll keep it at q3.
species_check: Zoom 4.4x head: pale yellow bill, glossy dark head, dark eye. Zoom 3.7x tail: broad fanned short tail, feet tucked at tail base. Zoom 5.4x wingtips: both complete but soft; noise and processing visible. Plumage fine-spangled belly. Sturnus vulgaris adult.

author: Jon Brinn (Flickr user jon.brinn352, https://www.flickr.com/people/126816719@N03/); photo title 'three's a crowd'
license: Public Domain Mark 1.0 (Flickr); no attribution required. Note: a mark, not a CC grant
symmetry_note: Phase: wings raised and spread, top of the downstroke or landing flare. Near-bilateral: half-spans 415 px vs 481 px (about 7 pct; left wing more raised and foreshortened). Body axis nearly vertical, bill up. Tail fully fanned and centred. Tip-to-tip 907 px. Frame is a crop containing only this bird (the original also holds two other starlings fighting at left). Backlit silhouette against pale cloudy-blue sky with soft cloud texture.
why_kept: The only near-symmetric true-ventral raised-wing frame with the body axis in the image plane; full wings and tail on plain sky.
downloaded_as: cropped from original (crop box x 1300-2700, y 500-1600 of 2769x1735), re-saved JPEG q97 4:4:4
species_check: PROBABLE, not certain: backlit silhouette, so colour cues are absent. Zoom 6.4x head: pointed bill, speckled throat and breast. Zoom 5.2x tail: short fan of about a dozen square-tipped feathers. Zoom 9.7x wingtips: left wing sharp with all primaries, right wing slightly soft. Spangled underparts, pointed bill, short fanned tail and triangular wings fit Sturnus vulgaris; the photo's own text does not name the species (found via the photographer's starling search).

author: Alex M Shepherd (Flickr user 137390807@N03, https://www.flickr.com/people/137390807@N03/)
license: CC0 1.0 Universal (Flickr 'Public Domain Dedication (CC0)'); no attribution required
subspecies_or_sex_if_stated: not stated (adult carrying food; caption 'Starling adult in flight 22 5 2025 2a'; taken 2025-05-22)
symmetry_note: LOW CONFIDENCE. Strong bank: bird is nearly in profile, the lower wing is fully extended (about 1180 px half-span) while the raised wing is foreshortened (about 450 px apparent), about 45 pct left/right difference. Not a bilateral view. Food in bill, legs dangle. Raised wingtip soft (motion). Tip-to-tip 2018 px, Feret 2305 px. Plain blue sky.
why_kept: Kept only as a pose-phase reference for early downstroke (one wing high, one low) and wing-feather arrangement; not usable for symmetric outline fitting.
species_check: Zoom 3.8x head: glossy black head, eye, bill with pale grub. Zoom 3.1x tail: fanned tail, spangled green-edged undertail coverts, pink feet. Zoom 5.4x wingtips: lower tip sharp, raised wing tips rounded and soft. Sturnus vulgaris adult.

why_kept: Pose-phase reference for mid-downstroke with wings near horizontal; roll and foreshortened body make it unsuitable for outline fitting.

author: Ralf Hüsges (Flickr https://www.flickr.com/people/184290238@N07, photo https://www.flickr.com/photos/ralf-huesges/54094247446/)
subspecies_or_sex_if_stated: not stated (spangled adult-type plumage; taken 2024-10-17; title 'Steigflug' = climbing flight)
symmetry_note: LOW CONFIDENCE, phase uncertain. Climbing flight: body pitched about 45 deg nose-up and banked, one wing long and swept back (half-span about 2065 px), the other short and tucked (about 470 px), about 63 pct difference. Tail fanned. Left outermost primaries motion-smeared. Image shows heavy sharpening/painterly edges (possible AI-style upscaling), so fine feather edges are not trustworthy. Tip-to-tip 2626 px. Plain blue sky.
why_kept: Kept as a swept-back (hand-back) wing-shape reference only; not symmetric, pose phase not certain (late upstroke or early downstroke).
species_check: Zoom 3.1x head: pointed dark bill, head and breast densely spotted white on black. Zoom 2.5x tail: dark fanned tail with buff-edged undertail coverts, edges painterly. Zoom 5.4x wingtips: left tip blurred, right tip sharp. Spangling and shape fit Sturnus vulgaris.
